_what_this_is: Offline search fixtures. Everything served from this file is fixture data; the run records source_mode=mock so it can never be presented as measured. Metadata for the anchor entries was copied from a recorded live response capture; descriptions are written here.
_matching: The query is lowercased and whitespace-collapsed, then a rule matches when every string in all_tokens occurs in it as a substring. empty_rules are checked first, then rules, then the generated fallback. Substring matching (not token equality) is deliberate: Korean queries agglutinate particles onto nouns.
_zero_results_are_a_signal: Only empty_rules return 0 results, and they exist for one reason: the cited source does not exist. Every other query gets something, because in this product an empty result set reads as 'the source is not real' and a coverage gap would become a false hallucination verdict.

results.title: Coffee consumption and health: umbrella review of meta-analyses of multiple health outcomes
results.description: Umbrella review of 201 meta-analyses of observational research and 17 of interventional research. Coffee consumption was more often associated with benefit than harm, with the largest relative reduction in all-cause mortality at three to four cups a day. The authors state the evidence is observational and that harm was seen in pregnancy and in women at risk of fracture.

results.title: Association of coffee drinking with total and cause-specific mortality.
results.description: Prospective cohort of more than 400,000 adults. After adjustment for tobacco smoking, coffee drinking was inversely associated with total mortality. The authors note the study is observational and cannot establish a causal relation.

results.title: Coffee, Caffeine, and Health Outcomes: An Umbrella Review.
results.description: Umbrella review of coffee and caffeine across health outcomes. Moderate consumption was associated with lower all-cause mortality; the authors emphasise that almost all of the underlying evidence is observational.

results.title: Coffee Consumption and Mortality Risk
results.description: Book chapter reviewing cohort evidence on coffee consumption and mortality, including the difficulty of separating coffee from correlated lifestyle factors.

results.title: Coffee Protocol v1
results.description: Deposited study protocol. No citation data is available for this record.

results.title: Association of Coffee Drinking with Total and Cause-Specific Mortality
results.description: Full text of the NIH-AARP cohort analysis reporting an inverse association between coffee drinking and total mortality after adjustment for smoking.

results.title: Coffee drinking timing and mortality in US adults | European Heart Journal
results.description: Cohort analysis reporting that the timing of coffee drinking, not only the amount, tracks with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.

results.title: Coffee Consumption Linked to Lower Risk of Death - News Center
results.description: University news item summarising a UK Biobank analysis that reported lower mortality among coffee drinkers, including drinkers of decaffeinated coffee.

results.title: Coffee consumption and all-cause and cause-specific mortality: a meta-analysis
results.description: Abstract record of a dose-response meta-analysis of prospective cohorts on coffee and mortality.

results.title: Vitamin D supplementation to prevent acute respiratory tract infections: systematic review and meta-analysis of individual participant data
results.description: Individual participant data meta-analysis of 25 randomised controlled trials. A protective effect was seen overall, but in subgroup analysis the benefit was confined to participants with baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D below 25 nmol/L. Participants with higher baseline levels showed no significant benefit.

results.title: Effect of vitamin D3 supplementation on upper respiratory tract infections in healthy adults: the VIDARIS randomized controlled trial
results.description: Randomised placebo-controlled trial in healthy adults. Monthly vitamin D3 did not reduce the incidence or severity of upper respiratory tract infections.

results.title: Vitamin D supplementation and respiratory infection: what the subgroup findings mean for the general population
results.description: Abstract record discussing why an overall protective estimate driven by a deficient subgroup does not license a general-population recommendation.

results.title: Green tea catechins and blood pressure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
results.description: Meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. Green tea consumption produced a statistically significant reduction in systolic and diastolic blood pressure of roughly 2 mmHg. The authors describe the effect as small and note heterogeneity between trials.

results.title: Effects of green tea consumption on blood pressure: an updated dose-response meta-analysis
results.description: Abstract record of a dose-response meta-analysis reporting a modest blood pressure reduction with green tea, larger in participants who were hypertensive at baseline.

results.title: 녹차 섭취와 혈압 변화에 대한 무작위 대조시험 메타분석
results.description: 무작위 대조시험을 종합한 메타분석 요약. 녹차 섭취군에서 수축기·이완기 혈압이 약 2 mmHg 낮아졌으나 연구 간 이질성이 크다고 보고한다.

results.title: 녹차와 혈압, 얼마나 낮아지나
results.description: 메타분석 결과를 인용해 녹차의 혈압 강하 효과가 통계적으로는 유의하지만 임상적으로는 작다고 정리한 기사.

results.title: "Drink at least eight glasses of water a day." Really? Is there scientific evidence for "8 x 8"?
results.description: Review searching for the origin of the eight-glasses rule. No scientific study supporting the 8 x 8 recommendation was found, and the author reports evidence that healthy adults meet their needs without it.
results.journal: American Journal of Physiology-Regulatory, Integrative and Comparative Physiology

results.title: Water intake and kidney function in healthy adults: what the trials show
results.description: Abstract record of a randomised trial of increased water intake in adults with chronic kidney disease, reporting no significant slowing of kidney function decline over one year.

results.description: Abstract record of a randomised trial of increased water intake in adults with chronic kidney disease, reporting no significant slowing of kidney function decline over one year.

results.title: Coffee consumption and health: umbrella review of meta-analyses of multiple health outcomes
results.description: The same umbrella review that reports the mortality benefit also reports harm in pregnancy: higher coffee consumption was associated with low birth weight, pregnancy loss and preterm birth, and with fracture risk in women.

results.title: Caffeine intake during pregnancy and adverse birth outcomes: dose-response meta-analysis
results.description: Abstract record reporting a dose-dependent association between maternal caffeine intake and low birth weight, with no clear safe threshold identified.

results.title: Association of Coffee Drinking With Mortality by Genetic Variation in Caffeine Metabolism: Findings From the UK Biobank
results.description: The inverse association between coffee and mortality was not modified by genetic variants that govern caffeine metabolism, which the authors read as evidence against a simple caffeine mechanism and as a reason to keep residual confounding in view.

results.title: Residual confounding in observational nutrition research
results.description: Abstract record on why smoking, income and health-seeking behaviour remain plausible explanations for diet-mortality associations in cohort studies.

results.title: Caffeine effects on sleep taken 0, 3, or 6 hours before going to bed
results.description: Randomised double-blind trial. Caffeine taken even six hours before bedtime significantly reduced total sleep time; the authors found no condition in which evening caffeine improved sleep.

results.title: Evening caffeine and slow wave sleep: a systematic review
results.description: Abstract record reporting that evening caffeine reduces slow wave sleep and lengthens sleep onset latency across trials.

results.title: Association Between Caffeine Intake and All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality: A Population-Based Prospective Cohort Study
results.description: Prospective cohort analysis of caffeine intake and mortality. The association was attenuated after adjustment for smoking and other lifestyle factors.

results.title: Coffee, tea, and caffeine intake and mortality in a pooled analysis of eight prospective cohort studies
results.description: Pooled cohort analysis reporting inverse associations for coffee and tea intake, with wide confidence intervals for the highest intake categories.

fallback._why: A query that matches no rule must not come back empty. Empty means 'this source does not exist' to the axis that checks existence, so an unmatched query would turn a coverage gap into a false hallucination verdict. These generated results are deterministic and deliberately neutral: they neither support nor contradict, so a fidelity judgement made on them lands on 'undecidable'.
